text: Never cooked or pressed, the long, cool, mostly lactic set is moulded, salted and left to ripen into a soft, acidic, creamy paste with live lactic bacteria. If left longer, natural moulds on the surface turn it creamy under the rind and give it a more pronounced taste.

steps.note: The curd is put into cylindrical plastic moulds, 10–14 cm across, for up to 2 days, to make cheeses of 250–400 g.
The cheese is ripened until natural moulds bloom on its surface: after 3–10 days it is fresh, after more than 10 days it is aged.
